message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. My girlfriend and I are both moderately overweight, and we've noticed we're getting even fatter. So, I pushed us to try losing weight. We started walking every day, cutting sugar, and eating better in reasonable quantities. It's been tough on her because she really enjoys eating until she's full. I'm the one trying to keep us on track, and I often have to call her out when she slips back into our old eating habits. Last weekend, we went to a wedding together. We were sitting next to each other with family members from both our families at the same table. Each table had its own food, so everyone could serve themselves. What happened next was that I watched my girlfriend fill her plate with all kinds of delicious food. I gave her a look, but she just shrugged it off, saying, "Yeah, I know, but we're at a wedding." I was slightly annoyed but tried to enjoy everyone's company. Later, when she finished, she asked me to pass her a big plate of shrimp rice so she could try some. That really bothered me, but I didn't want to argue right there. So, what I did was get the shrimp rice and proceed to fill her plate until it was literally overflowing a little bit. She stared at it, then got up and went outside alone. Everyone was staring at me, and I thought it was better to go outside too to talk to her. She told me she was humiliated and that I stepped out of line, acting like a controlling jerk. Now, the question is: Am I the asshole for taking a stand against her completely disregarding our agreed-upon diet? Hmm. Let me break this down. First, I pushed us to lose weight, which is a good intention. We made changes together, so there was an agreement. However, I'm the one who's more active in keeping us on track, which might mean I'm taking on more responsibility, but it could also come off as controlling. At the wedding, she filled her plate, and I gave her a look. She acknowledged it but chose to eat anyway. Then, when she asked for more, I reacted by overfilling her plate. That seems like a passive-aggressive way to express my frustration. It's not a constructive approach because it's public, which could embarrass her, and it's not solving the problem. I think the key points here are: 1. Did I handle the situation respectfully and constructively? 2. Was my reaction appropriate given the context? 3. Did I consider her feelings and the public setting? I didn't handle it well. Instead of addressing the issue privately or finding a kind way to remind her of our goals, I chose to make a scene by overfilling her plate. This could have made her feel humiliated and reinforced the idea that I'm controlling, which she already felt. Also, by doing this in front of others, I didn't just affect our relationship but also created an awkward situation for everyone else. It's important to communicate concerns privately, especially in sensitive situations like a wedding where emotions might be running high. So, in this case, I think I did come off as the asshole because my reaction was not appropriate, it was public, and it didn't help the situation. It probably made things worse between us and embarrassed her in front of others.
